## Explore Student Projects

Students have contributed to a range of research and education projects through
course-based research experiences and community collaboration.

```{=html}
<div class="card-grid">
  <article class="feature-card">
    <h3>Hands-on Microbiology</h3>
    <p>
      Students in MB 360 and LSC 170 explore <em>Delftia</em> through lab work,
      including spot-plate assays, and investigate its biology through scientific
      publications.
    </p>
    <p class="timeline-tags">
      <span class="tag-chip">MB 360</span>
      <span class="tag-chip">LSC 170</span>
      <span class="tag-chip">Lab Research</span>
    </p>
  </article>

  <article class="feature-card">
    <h3>Gold Recovery and E-Waste</h3>
    <p>
      Students and community annotators investigated how <em>Delftia</em>'s
      gold-biomineralizing abilities might contribute to recovering gold from
      electronic waste.
    </p>
    <p class="timeline-tags">
      <span class="tag-chip">Biotechnology</span>
      <span class="tag-chip">Sustainability</span>
      <span class="tag-chip">Literature Review</span>
    </p>
  </article>

  <article class="feature-card">
    <h3>Exploring <em>Delftia</em> as a Pathogen</h3>
    <p>
      Collaborative literature reviews and annotations examined published case
      studies of <em>Delftia acidovorans</em> infections and how this bacterium is
      identified in medical research.
    </p>
    <p class="timeline-tags">
      <span class="tag-chip">Literature Review</span>
      <span class="tag-chip">Collaborative Annotation</span>
    </p>
  </article>

  <article class="feature-card">
    <h3>WikiEDU and Science Communication</h3>
    <p>
      In 2020, 17 undergraduate volunteers took part in the Delftia WikiEDU
      program, working to improve access to information about <em>Delftia</em>
      on Wikipedia.
    </p>
    <p class="timeline-tags">
      <span class="tag-chip">WikiEDU</span>
      <span class="tag-chip">Science Communication</span>
    </p>
  </article>
</div>
```

::: {.research-spotlight}
::: {.research-spotlight-text}
### Student Research in Action

Course-based research experiences give students the opportunity to ask questions,
work with scientific evidence, and share what they learn. The projects above
reflect contributions to microbiology, biotechnology, and public access to
science.
